title: $T_{E,\Qlb}$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, a scheme $X$, a finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Qlb$ and a
bounded constructible complex $K$ of $E_X$-modules ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), the
complex $T_{E,\Qlb}K$ ([def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]) is a bounded constructible complex of
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$-modules.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], $T_{E,\Qlb}$ is the derived extension of scalars along $E_X\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$. The flatness statement [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat] gives preservation of finite limits by the underived extension, while [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] says extension is left adjoint to restriction and preserves finite colimits. Thus the extension is exact; [def-sfb-left-derived-exact] identifies its left derived functor with its termwise functor. The required general derived extension exists in precisely these module categories by [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar]. Flatness here holds for every scheme, as required by the general homology lemma. Applying [lem-sfb-extend-scalars-preserves-homology] to this coefficient map gives $H^n(T_{E,\Qlb}K)\cong\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}H^n(K)$ for every $n$. Since $K$ is bounded, this cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval, so $T_{E,\Qlb}K$ is bounded.

source.place: Proof paragraph, first clause: exactness, termwise computation and boundedness

proof.text: Write $R=E_X$, $B=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}$, and $A(M)=B\otimes_R M$. For any scheme morphism $g:Z\to X$, restriction commutes with this extension. Indeed the inverse image on abelian sheaves is strong monoidal by [def-sfb-finite-upper-star-monoidal] and is a left adjoint by [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction], hence takes the defining coequalizer of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] to the coequalizer for $g^{-1}B\otimes_{g^{-1}R}g^{-1}M$. For clarity, preservation of this coequalizer follows directly from the adjunction: maps from its inverse image to $N$ correspond to maps from the original coequalizer to $g_*N$, hence to maps from the original tensor target to $g_*N$ equalizing the two arrows; adjunction identifies these with maps from the pulled-back tensor target to $N$ equalizing the pulled-back arrows. This is precisely the coequalizer universal property. Identify $g^{-1}R\cong E_Z$ and $g^{-1}B\cong\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z}$ by the restriction convention of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The coefficient square of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] identifies the pulled-back map with $E_Z\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z}$. Under the module pullback formula of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] we have therefore obtained $g^*A(M)\cong\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z}\otimes_{E_Z}g^*M$. This applies both to strata and to objects of their pro-étale covers, and to affine opens of an arbitrary $X$.

source.place: Local presentations on strata: explicit inverse-image and coequalizer calculation

proof.text: Fix $n$ and put $M=H^n(K)$. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] and [sk-def-sfb-constructible], on each affine open choose a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes, and on every stratum a pro-étale cover on which $M$ is the cokernel of a finite matrix $C$ with entries in $E$. (If $X$ is qcqs one may use its global finite stratification.) Write a covering object as $V$. Step 2 identifies the restriction of $A(M)$ with $B_V\otimes_{E_V}M|_V$, where $B_V=\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,V}$. By [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] this functor preserves finite colimits, hence cokernels and finite sums. It takes $E_V$ to $B_V$: the maps $b\otimes r\mapsto b\,a_V(r)$ and $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ are inverse, since the balancing relation gives $b\otimes r=b\,a_V(r)\otimes1$. Thus it takes the matrix presentation $E_V^m\xrightarrow{C}E_V^r\to M|_V\to0$ to $B_V^m\xrightarrow{a(C)}B_V^r\to A(M)|_V\to0$. Its matrix entries are the images of the same scalar entries under $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, so this is a finite constant local model, not merely an arbitrary finite presentation. The same strata are constructible and the same covers suffice. Hence $A(H^n(K))$ is constructible on every required affine open, and globally in the qcqs case. Step 1 identifies this with $H^n(T_{E,\Qlb}K)$ and gives the same finite cohomology interval as $K$. The defining criterion of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] now proves the claimed bounded constructibility.

source.place: Final clause: finite scalar matrices survive extension, on the same strata and covers
